writeup: TIC 78186062 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.0009 days. Observations from TESS show a primary eclipse with a depth of 9.25% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal registers a detection significance of 98.3 in the BLS analysis, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 62.6, though the centroid offset of 4.5 arcsec from the target should be noted. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be previously unknown to the scientific literature. The machine-learning screening score of 0.39 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing system rather than instrumental noise or other false positive.
